subject.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles

question: Are process-local delete-wave reconstruction and potentially overlapping fresh-key wake retries acceptable trade-offs for fixing the top-level fan-out stall?
rationale: The patch and proof support the fix, but these two behaviors are deliberate session-state and delivery semantics; changing them would require a larger durable single-flight design rather than a mechanical contributor follow-up.

options.title: Accept bounded recovery trade-offs
options.body: Land the current design after refreshing the branch and confirming focused exact-head checks, accepting degraded restart reconstruction and prompt-bounded duplicate suppression.

options.title: Require durable single-flight recovery
options.body: Hold the PR until settled-wave facts survive restart and one lifecycle-owned wake run exclusively controls retry attempts.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded recovery trade-offs
recommendation.body: Land the current design after refreshing the branch and confirming focused exact-head checks, accepting degraded restart reconstruction and prompt-bounded duplicate suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work owns the announce continuation and registry lifecycle contracts that define whether these trade-offs are acceptable.
